title: The Lewis brothers Dude and Forstown
summary: Dude played trumpet and Forstown trombone; country-born, good players who could not read music.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: I asked you about the Lewis, the Lewis's, you said there were brothers, there was Foster Lewis and there was Dude Lewis?

Yeah. What was the Dude's name? Well, I'll tell you the truth, I know that wasn't the right name but it was the only name known by the musicians. They called one of them Dude, Dude was the trumpet player and Forstown was the trombone player.
Forstown Lewis. Oh, I thought it was Foster.

Well, that's what I'm saying. You see, that's forstown is Creole. Oh, I see. I see. Yeah. Forstown Lewis is the right name. But now, I don't know if Dude had another name but that was his only known name to the musicians. Dude, you see, because all the musicians called him.
You say Dude was the trumpet player?

Dude was the trumpet player and Forstown was the trombone player. Trombone player. And a good one too. He couldn't read but boy, he had a tone and a trombone. Yes, sir. Yeah, that was two brothers was good for say country boys and just liked his self. I mean, if Dude was living now, he would be right in the demands of the style of trumpet playing that they want to be. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. He played just on that style and type, you know?
You say they were from the country somewhere.
Yeah, they came from, I don't know exactly, I don't know if they, what they were born in the class, I know it's in the country. Yeah, they came from the country boys.
Yeah, they came from the country boys.
And they didn't learn music here, they liked music in the country, they come here playing. Of course they had been around here for a number of years but originally their home is in the country.
